```{r}
#| label: review-openalex
#| output: false
# OpenAlex searches titles and abstracts. Abstracts are publisher text and are
# written only under 02.inputs/searches, which is not committed; the committed
# hits file carries bibliographic fields alone.
pending <- pending_queries("openalex-")
if (nrow(pending) > 0) {
  abstract_text <- function(inv) {
    if (is.null(inv)) return(NA_character_)
    pos <- unlist(inv, use.names = FALSE)
    words <- rep(names(inv), lengths(inv))
    paste(words[order(pos)], collapse = " ")
  }
  search_oa <- function(question, route, concepts, cap = 3000) {
    query <- boolean_query(concepts)
    # Pages are numbered, because paging past the first page with a cursor
    # needs an API key as of 2026-10-14 and numbered pages do not.
    works <- list(); page <- 1; total <- NA; err <- NA
    repeat {
      # OpenAlex works endpoint, https://docs.openalex.org/api-entities/works/search-works
      resp <- httr2::request("https://api.openalex.org/works") |>
        httr2::req_url_query(filter = paste0("title_and_abstract.search:", query, ",from_publication_date:1987-01-01"),
                             select = "id,doi,title,publication_year,primary_location,type,cited_by_count,abstract_inverted_index",
                             `per-page` = 200, page = page, mailto = "seamusrobertmurphy@gmail.com") |>
        httr2::req_retry(max_tries = 6) |>
        httr2::req_error(is_error = \(r) FALSE) |>
        httr2::req_perform()
      if (httr2::resp_status(resp) != 200) { err <- paste("HTTP", httr2::resp_status(resp)); break }
      body <- httr2::resp_body_json(resp)
      total <- body$meta$count; page <- page + 1
      works <- c(works, body$results)
      if (length(works) >= total || length(body$results) == 0 || length(works) >= cap) break
    }
    rows <- works |>
      purrr::map(\(w) tibble::tibble(
        openalex = w$id %||% NA_character_,
        doi = stringr::str_remove(w$doi %||% NA_character_, "^https://doi.org/"),
        title = w$title %||% NA_character_, year = w$publication_year %||% NA_integer_,
        venue = w$primary_location$source$display_name %||% NA_character_,
        type = w$type %||% NA_character_, citations = w$cited_by_count %||% NA_integer_,
        abstract = abstract_text(w$abstract_inverted_index))) |>
      purrr::list_rbind()
    if (nrow(rows) == 0) rows <- tibble::tibble(doi = character(), title = character(), abstract = character())
    list(hits = dplyr::mutate(rows, question, route = paste0("openalex-", route), .before = 1),
         log = tibble::tibble(strand = "openalex", route = paste0("openalex-", route), query, date = as.character(Sys.Date()),
                              retrieved = nrow(rows), reported_total = total, cap, capped = isTRUE(total > cap), error = err))
  }
  runs <- purrr::pmap(pending, search_oa)
  oa <- purrr::map(runs, "hits") |> purrr::list_rbind()
  dir.create("../02.inputs/searches", showWarnings = FALSE)
  if (nrow(oa) > 0) {
    append_csv(oa, "../02.inputs/searches/review-openalex-records.csv")
    append_csv(dplyr::select(oa, -abstract), "../02.inputs/derived/review-openalex-hits.csv")
  }
  append_csv(purrr::map(runs, "log") |> purrr::list_rbind(), search_log_path)
}
```

```{r}
#| label: review-ads
#| output: false
# NASA ADS searches abstracts with a personal token read from outside the
# repository. The token "trend" is a stopword in ADS, so any query carrying it
# is run without that concept and logged as such.
pending <- pending_queries("ads-")
if (nrow(pending) > 0) {
  token_file <- path.expand("~/.ads/dev_key")
  search_ads <- function(question, route, concepts, cap = 2000) {
    groups <- stringr::str_split_1(concepts, " AND ")
    dropped <- groups[stringr::str_detect(groups, "^trend")]
    groups <- groups[!stringr::str_detect(groups, "^trend")]
    query <- paste0("abs:", boolean_query(paste(groups, collapse = " AND ")), " year:1987-")
    rows <- tibble::tibble(); total <- NA; err <- NA; start <- 0
    if (!file.exists(token_file)) err <- "no token" else repeat {
      # NASA ADS search API, https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/help/api/api-docs.html
      resp <- httr2::request("https://api.adsabs.harvard.edu/v1/search/query") |>
        httr2::req_headers(Authorization = paste("Bearer", readLines(token_file, warn = FALSE)[1])) |>
        httr2::req_url_query(q = query, fl = "bibcode,title,year,pub,doi,doctype,abstract", rows = 200, start = start) |>
        httr2::req_retry(max_tries = 4) |>
        httr2::req_error(is_error = \(r) FALSE) |>
        httr2::req_perform()
      if (httr2::resp_status(resp) != 200) { err <- paste("HTTP", httr2::resp_status(resp)); break }
      body <- httr2::resp_body_json(resp)$response
      total <- body$numFound
      page <- body$docs |>
        purrr::map(\(d) tibble::tibble(bibcode = d$bibcode %||% NA_character_, doi = unlist(d$doi)[1] %||% NA_character_,
                                       title = unlist(d$title)[1] %||% NA_character_, year = as.integer(d$year %||% NA),
                                       venue = d$pub %||% NA_character_, type = d$doctype %||% NA_character_,
                                       abstract = d$abstract %||% NA_character_)) |>
        purrr::list_rbind()
      rows <- dplyr::bind_rows(rows, page)
      start <- start + 200
      if (nrow(page) == 0 || start >= total || nrow(rows) >= cap) break
    }
    if (nrow(rows) == 0) rows <- tibble::tibble(doi = character(), title = character(), abstract = character())
    list(hits = dplyr::mutate(rows, question, route = paste0("ads-", route), .before = 1),
         log = tibble::tibble(strand = "ads", route = paste0("ads-", route), query, date = as.character(Sys.Date()),
                              retrieved = nrow(rows), reported_total = total, cap, capped = isTRUE(total > cap),
                              error = dplyr::coalesce(err, if (length(dropped)) paste("stopword concept dropped:", dropped) else NA)))
  }
  runs <- purrr::pmap(pending, search_ads)
  ads <- purrr::map(runs, "hits") |> purrr::list_rbind()
  if (nrow(ads) > 0) {
    append_csv(ads, "../02.inputs/searches/review-ads-records.csv")
    append_csv(dplyr::select(ads, -abstract), "../02.inputs/derived/review-ads-hits.csv")
  }
  append_csv(purrr::map(runs, "log") |> purrr::list_rbind(), search_log_path)
}
```

```{r}
#| label: review-semantic-scholar
#| output: false
# Semantic Scholar is the index the library protocol names. Without a key it
# rate limits, so a refusal is logged against the query rather than stopping
# the render, and the log row says which strand is missing. A key, when one is
# held, is read from outside the repository and sent as a header.
pending <- pending_queries("s2-")
if (nrow(pending) > 0) {
  key_file <- path.expand("~/.s2/api_key")
  s2_key <- if (file.exists(key_file)) readLines(key_file, warn = FALSE)[1] else NULL
  search_s2 <- function(question, route, concepts, cap = 3000) {
    query <- boolean_query(concepts, or = " | ", and = " + ")
    papers <- list(); token <- NULL; total <- NA; err <- NA
    repeat {
      # Semantic Scholar Academic Graph bulk search, https://api.semanticscholar.org/api-docs/graph#tag/Paper-Data/operation/get_graph_paper_bulk_search
      resp <- httr2::request("https://api.semanticscholar.org/graph/v1/paper/search/bulk") |>
        httr2::req_url_query(query = query, year = "1987-", fields = "title,year,venue,externalIds,citationCount,publicationTypes", token = token) |>
        httr2::req_headers(`x-api-key` = s2_key) |>
        httr2::req_throttle(rate = 1 / 2) |>
        httr2::req_retry(max_tries = 3, backoff = \(i) 5 * i) |>
        httr2::req_error(is_error = \(r) FALSE) |>
        httr2::req_perform()
      if (httr2::resp_status(resp) != 200) { err <- paste("HTTP", httr2::resp_status(resp)); break }
      body <- httr2::resp_body_json(resp)
      total <- body$total; token <- body$token
      papers <- c(papers, body$data)
      if (is.null(token) || length(papers) >= cap) break
    }
    works <- papers |>
      purrr::map(\(w) tibble::tibble(doi = w$externalIds$DOI %||% NA_character_, title = w$title %||% NA_character_, year = w$year %||% NA_integer_, venue = w$venue %||% NA_character_, type = paste(unlist(w$publicationTypes), collapse = " "), citations = w$citationCount %||% NA_integer_)) |>
      purrr::list_rbind()
    if (nrow(works) == 0) works <- tibble::tibble(doi = character(), title = character())
    list(hits = dplyr::mutate(works, question, route = paste0("s2-", route), .before = 1),
         log = tibble::tibble(strand = "semantic-scholar", route = paste0("s2-", route), query, date = as.character(Sys.Date()), retrieved = nrow(works), reported_total = total, cap, capped = isTRUE(total > cap), error = err))
  }
  runs <- purrr::pmap(pending, search_s2)
  s2 <- purrr::map(runs, "hits") |> purrr::list_rbind()
  if (nrow(s2) > 0) append_csv(s2, "../02.inputs/derived/review-s2-hits.csv")
  append_csv(purrr::map(runs, "log") |> purrr::list_rbind(), search_log_path)
}
```

```{r}
#| label: review-chase
#| output: false
# One round of backward and forward chasing from the central records, through
# OpenAlex, which lists both the references of a work and the works citing it.
central <- c("10.4095/st000101", "10.1175/waf-d-23-0226.1", "10.1016/j.agrformet.2018.07.005",
             "10.1007/s10584-012-0667-2", "10.1071/wf17008", "10.1071/wf11088")
if (length(central) > 0 && !file.exists("../02.inputs/derived/review-chase-hits.csv")) {
  oa_get <- function(url, query = list()) {
    resp <- httr2::request(url) |> httr2::req_url_query(!!!query, mailto = "seamusrobertmurphy@gmail.com") |>
      httr2::req_retry(max_tries = 6) |> httr2::req_error(is_error = \(r) FALSE) |> httr2::req_perform()
    if (httr2::resp_status(resp) != 200) return(NULL)
    httr2::resp_body_json(resp)
  }
  as_row <- \(w) tibble::tibble(openalex = w$id %||% NA_character_, doi = stringr::str_remove(w$doi %||% NA_character_, "^https://doi.org/"), title = w$title %||% NA_character_, year = w$publication_year %||% NA_integer_, venue = w$primary_location$source$display_name %||% NA_character_)
  chase <- function(seed_doi) {
    # OpenAlex works endpoint, https://docs.openalex.org/api-entities/works
    seed <- oa_get(paste0("https://api.openalex.org/works/https://doi.org/", seed_doi))
    if (is.null(seed)) return(tibble::tibble(seed = seed_doi, route = "chase", error = "seed not found"))
    refs <- if (length(seed$referenced_works)) oa_get("https://api.openalex.org/works", list(filter = paste0("ids.openalex:", paste(basename(unlist(seed$referenced_works)), collapse = "|")), `per-page` = 200, select = "id,doi,title,publication_year,primary_location")) else NULL
    cites <- oa_get("https://api.openalex.org/works", list(filter = paste0("cites:", basename(seed$id)), `per-page` = 200, select = "id,doi,title,publication_year,primary_location"))
    dplyr::bind_rows(
      purrr::map(refs$results %||% list(), as_row) |> purrr::list_rbind() |> dplyr::mutate(route = "chase-references"),
      purrr::map(cites$results %||% list(), as_row) |> purrr::list_rbind() |> dplyr::mutate(route = "chase-citations")
    ) |> dplyr::mutate(seed = seed_doi, .before = 1)
  }
  chased <- purrr::map(central, chase) |> purrr::list_rbind()
  readr::write_csv(chased, "../02.inputs/derived/review-chase-hits.csv")
  readr::read_csv("../02.inputs/derived/review-search-log.csv", col_types = readr::cols(.default = "c")) |>
    dplyr::bind_rows(chased |> dplyr::count(seed, route, name = "retrieved") |>
      dplyr::transmute(strand = "openalex-chase", route = paste(route, seed), query = seed, date = as.character(Sys.Date()),
                       retrieved = as.character(retrieved), reported_total = retrieved, cap = NA, capped = "FALSE", error = NA)) |>
    readr::write_csv("../02.inputs/derived/review-search-log.csv")
}
```

```{r}
#| label: review-records
#| output: false
# One row per unique record across every strand. A record already cited by this
# manuscript is marked, by DOI against the bibliography, so screening can see
# what the earlier reading had reached.
records_path <- "../02.inputs/derived/review-records.csv"
read_hits <- \(p) if (file.exists(p)) readr::read_csv(p, col_types = readr::cols(.default = "c")) else tibble::tibble()
bib <- paste(readLines("../04.references/references.bib", warn = FALSE), collapse = " ")
bib_dois <- stringr::str_to_lower(unlist(stringr::str_extract_all(bib, "10\\.[0-9]{4,9}/[^\\s,}\"]+")))
fresh <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  read_hits("../02.inputs/derived/review-store-hits.csv"),
  read_hits("../02.inputs/derived/review-openalex-hits.csv"),
  read_hits("../02.inputs/derived/review-ads-hits.csv"),
  read_hits("../02.inputs/derived/review-s2-hits.csv"),
  # The Consensus route was run by hand through the session's search tool on
  # 2026-10-14, three results per query, and its hits file was typed from them.
  read_hits("../02.inputs/derived/review-consensus-hits.csv"),
  read_hits("../02.inputs/derived/review-chase-hits.csv") |> dplyr::mutate(question = "chase")
) |>
  dplyr::mutate(doi = stringr::str_to_lower(doi),
                id = dplyr::coalesce(doi, stringr::str_squish(stringr::str_to_lower(stringr::str_replace_all(title, "[^[:alnum:] ]", " "))))) |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(id), id != "") |>
  dplyr::summarise(.by = id, doi = dplyr::first(stats::na.omit(doi)), title = dplyr::first(stats::na.omit(title)), year = dplyr::first(stats::na.omit(year)), venue = dplyr::first(stats::na.omit(venue)), type = dplyr::first(stats::na.omit(type)), questions = paste(sort(unique(question)), collapse = " "), routes = paste(sort(unique(route)), collapse = " "), duplicates_merged = dplyr::n(), key = dplyr::first(stats::na.omit(key)), source_note = dplyr::first(stats::na.omit(source_note))) |>
  dplyr::mutate(cited = dplyr::if_else(!is.na(doi) & doi %in% bib_dois, "yes", "no")) |>
  dplyr::mutate(dplyr::across(dplyr::everything(), as.character))
if (!file.exists(records_path)) {
  fresh |>
    dplyr::mutate(decision = NA, reason = NA, full_text = NA) |>
    readr::write_csv(records_path, na = "")
} else {
  # A later pass adds its records as new rows and refreshes the questions and
  # routes of the rows it found again. Every decision, reason, full text flag,
  # note and hand typed key already in the table is kept, and a row added by
  # hand, such as a grey literature record, is kept as it stands.
  old <- readr::read_csv(records_path, col_types = readr::cols(.default = "c"))
  kept <- old |> dplyr::select(id, old_key = key, old_source_note = source_note, decision, reason, full_text, dplyr::any_of("note"))
  merged <- dplyr::bind_rows(
    fresh |>
      dplyr::left_join(kept, by = "id") |>
      dplyr::mutate(key = dplyr::coalesce(old_key, key), source_note = dplyr::coalesce(old_source_note, source_note)) |>
      dplyr::select(-old_key, -old_source_note),
    old |> dplyr::filter(!id %in% fresh$id)
  )
  merged <- dplyr::mutate(merged, dplyr::across(dplyr::everything(), as.character))
  if (!identical(merged, old)) readr::write_csv(merged, records_path, na = "")
}
```

```{python}
#| label: review-screening-pack
#| output: false
"""Build the title-and-abstract screening batches for the 2026-10-13 literature review.

Reads the committed screening table 02.inputs/derived/review-records.csv, applies the
document-type rule of the review protocol (records of an ineligible type are excluded by
rule with the code not-research), attaches each remaining record's abstract from the
uncommitted search files under 02.inputs/searches, fetches the abstract from OpenAlex by
DOI where no search file holds it, and writes one batch per question under
02.inputs/searches/review-batches/. Abstracts are publisher text and never leave
02.inputs/searches. Runs only while a record has no decision or stands undecided, and
names each batch by the day it was built so an earlier pass's batches are never
overwritten.
"""
import csv, json, os, sys, time, urllib.parse, urllib.request

ROOT = os.path.abspath("..")
DERIVED = os.path.join(ROOT, "02.inputs", "derived")
SEARCHES = os.path.join(ROOT, "02.inputs", "searches")
BATCHES = os.path.join(SEARCHES, "review-batches")
MAILTO = "seamusrobertmurphy@gmail.com"
INELIGIBLE = {"abstract", "conference-abstract", "dataset", "peer-review", "paratext", "erratum", "editorial", "letter", "other"}

def read(p):
    with open(p, encoding="utf-8", newline="") as f:
        return list(csv.DictReader(f))

def write(p, rows, fields):
    with open(p, "w", encoding="utf-8", newline="") as f:
        w = csv.DictWriter(f, fieldnames=fields); w.writeheader(); w.writerows(rows)

def abstract_from_inverted(inv):
    if not inv: return ""
    pos = []
    for word, idx in inv.items():
        for i in idx: pos.append((i, word))
    return " ".join(w for _, w in sorted(pos))

def fetch_openalex(dois):
    out = {}
    for i in range(0, len(dois), 50):
        chunk = dois[i:i + 50]
        # OpenAlex works endpoint, https://docs.openalex.org/api-entities/works
        url = "https://api.openalex.org/works?" + urllib.parse.urlencode({
            "filter": "doi:" + "|".join(chunk), "per-page": 50,
            "select": "doi,abstract_inverted_index,type", "mailto": MAILTO})
        for attempt in range(4):
            try:
                with urllib.request.urlopen(url, timeout=60) as r:
                    body = json.load(r)
                break
            except Exception as e:
                time.sleep(3 * (attempt + 1)); body = {"results": []}
        for w in body.get("results", []):
            d = (w.get("doi") or "").replace("https://doi.org/", "").lower()
            out[d] = (abstract_from_inverted(w.get("abstract_inverted_index")), w.get("type") or "")
        time.sleep(0.2)
    return out

def main():
    records = read(os.path.join(DERIVED, "review-records.csv"))
    abstracts = {}
    for name in ("review-openalex-records.csv", "review-ads-records.csv"):
        p = os.path.join(SEARCHES, name)
        if not os.path.exists(p): continue
        for r in read(p):
            key = (r.get("doi") or "").lower() or r["title"].lower()
            if r.get("abstract") and r["abstract"] != "NA": abstracts.setdefault(key, r["abstract"])
    need = [r["doi"] for r in records if r["doi"] and r["doi"].lower() not in abstracts]
    fetched = fetch_openalex(need)
    for d, (a, t) in fetched.items():
        if a: abstracts[d] = a
    n_rule = 0
    for r in records:
        if not r["type"] and r["doi"] and r["doi"].lower() in fetched:
            r["type"] = fetched[r["doi"].lower()][1]
        if r["type"] in INELIGIBLE and (not r["decision"] or r["decision"] == "undecided"):
            r["decision"], r["reason"] = "exclude", "not-research"; n_rule += 1
    write(os.path.join(DERIVED, "review-records.csv"), records, list(records[0].keys()))
    os.makedirs(BATCHES, exist_ok=True)
    batches = {}
    for r in records:
        if r["decision"] and r["decision"] != "undecided": continue
        key = (r["doi"] or "").lower() or r["id"]
        row = {"id": r["id"], "doi": r["doi"], "title": r["title"], "year": r["year"], "venue": r["venue"],
               "type": r["type"], "questions": r["questions"], "cited": r["cited"],
               "abstract": abstracts.get(key, "")}
        q = r["questions"].split()[0] if r["questions"] else "chase"
        batches.setdefault(q, []).append(row)
    fields = ["id", "doi", "title", "year", "venue", "type", "questions", "cited", "abstract"]
    tag = "" if not os.path.isdir(BATCHES) or not os.listdir(BATCHES) else "-" + time.strftime("%Y-%m-%d")
    for q, rows in batches.items():
        if q == "chase" and len(rows) > 220:
            half = (len(rows) + 1) // 2
            write(os.path.join(BATCHES, f"chase-a{tag}.csv"), rows[:half], fields)
            write(os.path.join(BATCHES, f"chase-b{tag}.csv"), rows[half:], fields)
        else:
            write(os.path.join(BATCHES, f"{q}{tag}.csv"), rows, fields)
    print("records", len(records), "excluded by type rule", n_rule,
          "to screen", sum(len(v) for v in batches.values()),
          "with abstract", sum(1 for v in batches.values() for r in v if r["abstract"]))
    for q, rows in batches.items(): print(" ", q, len(rows))

with open(os.path.join(DERIVED, "review-records.csv"), encoding="utf-8", newline="") as f:
    open_rows = [r for r in csv.DictReader(f) if not r.get("decision") or r["decision"] == "undecided"]
if open_rows:
    main()
```

```{python}
#| label: review-screening-merge
#| output: false
"""Merge the screening decisions of the 2026-10-13 literature review into the screening table.

Reads every decisions-*.csv under 02.inputs/searches/review-batches/, checks that each id
was decided exactly once and that every exclusion carries a code from the protocol, and
writes decision, reason and note into 02.inputs/derived/review-records.csv. A record that
already carries a decision in the table (hand-found records, records excluded by the
document-type rule) keeps it, and a record standing undecided takes the decision of a
later batch. Runs only while a row of the table has no decision or stands undecided.
"""
import csv, glob, os, sys

ROOT = os.path.abspath("..")
TABLE = os.path.join(ROOT, "02.inputs", "derived", "review-records.csv")
BATCHES = os.path.join(ROOT, "02.inputs", "searches", "review-batches")
CODES = {"off-topic", "wrong-population", "wrong-concept", "not-research", "out-of-window", "not-english", "duplicate"}

def main():
    with open(TABLE, encoding="utf-8", newline="") as f:
        rows = list(csv.DictReader(f))
    fields = list(rows[0].keys())
    if "note" not in fields: fields.append("note")
    decided = {}
    for p in sorted(glob.glob(os.path.join(BATCHES, "decisions-*.csv"))):
        with open(p, encoding="utf-8", newline="") as f:
            for d in csv.DictReader(f):
                if d["decision"] not in {"include", "exclude", "undecided"}:
                    sys.exit(f"bad decision {d['decision']!r} for {d['id']} in {p}")
                if d["decision"] == "exclude" and d["reason"] not in CODES:
                    sys.exit(f"bad reason {d['reason']!r} for {d['id']} in {p}")
                if d["id"] in decided:
                    # A later batch may settle a record an earlier batch left
                    # undecided; two settled decisions for one record stop the render.
                    if decided[d["id"]]["decision"] == "undecided":
                        decided[d["id"]] = d
                    elif d["decision"] != "undecided":
                        sys.exit(f"id decided twice: {d['id']} in {p}")
                    continue
                decided[d["id"]] = d
    n_set = 0
    for r in rows:
        r.setdefault("note", "")
        if r.get("decision") and r["decision"] != "undecided":
            continue
        d = decided.get(r["id"])
        if d and d["decision"] != "undecided":
            r["decision"], r["reason"], r["note"] = d["decision"], d["reason"], d.get("note", ""); n_set += 1
        elif d and not r.get("decision"):
            r["decision"], r["reason"], r["note"] = d["decision"], d["reason"], d.get("note", ""); n_set += 1
    missing = [r["id"] for r in rows if not r.get("decision")]
    with open(TABLE, "w", encoding="utf-8", newline="") as f:
        w = csv.DictWriter(f, fieldnames=fields); w.writeheader(); w.writerows(rows)
    from collections import Counter
    print("decisions merged", n_set, "| undecided rows left without any decision", len(missing))
    print("by decision", Counter(r["decision"] for r in rows).most_common())
    print("by reason", Counter(r["reason"] for r in rows if r["decision"] == "exclude").most_common())
    if missing: print("first missing ids", missing[:10])

with open(TABLE, encoding="utf-8", newline="") as f:
    undecided_rows = [r for r in csv.DictReader(f) if not r.get("decision") or r["decision"] == "undecided"]
if undecided_rows:
    main()
```

```{python}
#| label: review-fulltext-fetch
#| output: false
"""Fetch full texts for the included records of the literature review.

For every row of 02.inputs/derived/review-records.csv with decision include and a DOI, tries
the routes of the review protocol in order, the publisher's DOI landing page (its
citation_pdf_url tag), OpenAlex's best open access location, Unpaywall's best open access
location, which covers institutional repositories, and the Internet Archive's closest
capture of the PDF address, and saves the first PDF that answers into
04.references/literature/review/, which is not committed. Writes one row per record to
02.inputs/derived/review-fulltext-log.csv with the route that answered, the routes tried
and the outcome, so the count of records whose full text could not be obtained is
measured rather than estimated. The session's browser is the last route and is never run
from here. Downloaded files are untrusted data and nothing is executed from that folder.
Runs while an included record has no row in the log, or while the log predates the route
column, and then retries every record not yet saved.
"""
import csv, html, json, os, re, time, urllib.parse, urllib.request

ROOT = os.path.abspath("..")
TABLE = os.path.join(ROOT, "02.inputs", "derived", "review-records.csv")
LOG = os.path.join(ROOT, "02.inputs", "derived", "review-fulltext-log.csv")
OUT = os.path.join(ROOT, "04.references", "literature", "review")
MAILTO = "seamusrobertmurphy@gmail.com"
UA = "forest-fire-index-trends review fetch (mailto:" + MAILTO + ")"
FIELDS = ["id", "doi", "year", "title", "url", "file", "status", "route", "routes_tried", "date"]

def get(url, accept="*/*", timeout=60):
    req = urllib.request.Request(url, headers={"User-Agent": "Mozilla/5.0 " + UA, "Accept": accept})
    with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=timeout) as r:
        return r.read(), r.geturl()

def get_json(url):
    data, _ = get(url, "application/json")
    return json.loads(data)

def download(url, path):
    data, _ = get(url, "application/pdf", 90)
    if not data.startswith(b"%PDF"):
        return "not a pdf"
    with open(path, "wb") as f:
        f.write(data)
    # Some publishers answer the citation_pdf_url tag with a first page preview of one or
    # two pages rather than the article. Such a file is removed and the next route tried.
    try:
        from pypdf import PdfReader
        if len(PdfReader(path).pages) <= 2:
            os.remove(path)
            return "preview only"
    except Exception:
        pass
    return "saved"

def route_landing(doi):
    # Publisher landing page reached through the DOI resolver, https://doi.org
    page, final = get("https://doi.org/" + urllib.parse.quote(doi), "text/html")
    m = re.search(rb'<meta[^>]+name="citation_pdf_url"[^>]+content="([^"]+)"', page) or \
        re.search(rb'<meta[^>]+content="([^"]+)"[^>]+name="citation_pdf_url"', page)
    return html.unescape(m.group(1).decode("utf-8", "replace")) if m else ""

def route_openalex(doi):
    # OpenAlex works endpoint, https://docs.openalex.org/api-entities/works
    w = get_json("https://api.openalex.org/works/https://doi.org/" + urllib.parse.quote(doi) + "?mailto=" + MAILTO)
    loc = w.get("best_oa_location") or {}
    return loc.get("pdf_url") or (w.get("open_access") or {}).get("oa_url") or ""

def route_unpaywall(doi):
    # Unpaywall REST API, https://unpaywall.org/products/api
    w = get_json("https://api.unpaywall.org/v2/" + urllib.parse.quote(doi) + "?email=" + MAILTO)
    loc = w.get("best_oa_location") or {}
    return loc.get("url_for_pdf") or loc.get("url") or ""

def route_archive(doi, urls):
    # Internet Archive Wayback availability API, https://archive.org/help/wayback_api.php
    for u in [x for x in urls if x] + ["https://doi.org/" + doi]:
        w = get_json("https://archive.org/wayback/available?url=" + urllib.parse.quote(u, safe=""))
        snap = (w.get("archived_snapshots") or {}).get("closest") or {}
        if snap.get("available") and snap.get("url"):
            return snap["url"].replace("http://", "https://", 1)
    return ""

def wanted_rows():
    # Every included record with a DOI, and every cited key the manuscript still rests
    # on an abstract for, whose DOI is read from the bibliography.
    with open(TABLE, encoding="utf-8", newline="") as f:
        rows = [r for r in csv.DictReader(f) if r["decision"] == "include" and r["doi"]]
    have = {r["doi"].lower() for r in rows}
    bib = open(os.path.join(ROOT, "04.references", "references.bib"), encoding="utf-8").read()
    key2doi = {}
    for m in re.finditer(r"@\w+\{\s*([^,\s]+)\s*,", bib):
        nxt = bib.find("\n@", m.end()); body = bib[m.end(): nxt if nxt > 0 else len(bib)]
        d = re.search(r"doi\s*=\s*[{\"]([^}\"]+)[}\"]", body, re.I)
        if d: key2doi[m.group(1)] = d.group(1).strip().lower()
    with open(os.path.join(ROOT, "02.inputs", "derived", "literature-cited.csv"), encoding="utf-8", newline="") as f:
        for c in csv.DictReader(f):
            d = key2doi.get(c["key"])
            if c["fulltext_read"].lower() == "false" and d and d not in have:
                rows.append({"id": d, "doi": d, "year": "", "title": "cited key " + c["key"], "decision": "include"}); have.add(d)
    return rows

def main():
    os.makedirs(OUT, exist_ok=True)
    rows = wanted_rows()
    done = {}
    if os.path.exists(LOG):
        with open(LOG, encoding="utf-8", newline="") as f:
            done = {r["doi"]: {k: r.get(k, "") for k in FIELDS} for r in csv.DictReader(f)}
    for r in rows:
        if r["doi"] in done and done[r["doi"]]["status"] == "saved":
            continue
        name = re.sub(r"[^A-Za-z0-9._-]", "_", r["doi"]) + ".pdf"
        path = os.path.join(OUT, name)
        status, url, route, tried = "", "", "", []
        if os.path.exists(path):
            status, route = "saved", "file present"
        else:
            urls = []
            for route_name, finder in (("landing", lambda: route_landing(r["doi"])),
                                       ("openalex", lambda: route_openalex(r["doi"])),
                                       ("unpaywall", lambda: route_unpaywall(r["doi"])),
                                       ("archive", lambda: route_archive(r["doi"], urls))):
                try:
                    url = finder()
                except Exception as e:
                    tried.append(route_name + " failed " + str(e)[:60]); continue
                if not url:
                    tried.append(route_name + " no copy"); continue
                urls.append(url)
                try:
                    status = download(url, path)
                except Exception as e:
                    status = "download failed " + str(e)[:80]
                tried.append(route_name + " " + status[:40])
                if status == "saved":
                    route = route_name; break
                time.sleep(0.3)
            if status != "saved":
                status = "no copy reached" if not status else status
        done[r["doi"]] = {"id": r["id"], "doi": r["doi"], "year": r["year"], "title": r["title"][:120], "url": url,
                          "file": name if status == "saved" else "", "status": status, "route": route,
                          "routes_tried": "; ".join(tried), "date": time.strftime("%Y-%m-%d")}
        time.sleep(0.3)
    with open(LOG, "w", encoding="utf-8", newline="") as f:
        w = csv.DictWriter(f, fieldnames=FIELDS); w.writeheader(); w.writerows(done.values())
    from collections import Counter
    print(Counter((v["status"][:20], v["route"]) for v in done.values()).most_common())

def pending_includes():
    wanted = {r["doi"] for r in wanted_rows()}
    logged, old_format = set(), False
    if os.path.exists(LOG):
        with open(LOG, encoding="utf-8", newline="") as f:
            rd = csv.DictReader(f); logged = {r["doi"] for r in rd}; old_format = "route" not in rd.fieldnames
    return (wanted - logged) or old_format

if pending_includes():
    main()
```


The literature behind the expectations in the Introduction was gathered under a written protocol frozen on 13 and extended on 14 October 2026. The protocol was run on the author's reference store, OpenAlex, NASA ADS, Semantic Scholar and Consensus, with citation chasing through OpenAlex and hand searches of the Canadian Forest Service, BC Wildfire Service and Natural Resources Canada publication stores. The searches (@fig-review-flow) retrieved `r n_fmt(review_counts$Records[1])` records, `r n_fmt(review_counts$Records[2])` of them unique, of which `r n_fmt(review_counts$Records[3])` were excluded on title and abstract, `r review_counts$Records[5]` were retained and `r review_counts$Records[4]` were read in full by one reader. NASA ADS treated trend as a stopword, so that strand was under-searched for the first question. For the novelty question every reading note was searched on 19 October 2026 for the names of the 2025 update. Neither of the two works OpenAlex listed as citing the report compared it with the 1987 System on an observed record.

## A.2 Implementation Checks {.unnumbered}

```{r}
#| label: tbl-verify
#| tbl-cap: "Verification of the FWI1987 implementation. The first block compares it against the CRAN package cffdrs over the Petawawa Research Forest test record. The second compares it against the FWI1987 codes BC Wildfire Service computed operationally at these stations, pooled over all kept station-seasons."
val <- read.csv(file.path(derived, "fwi1987-validation.csv"),
                stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
opc <- read.csv(file.path(derived, "fwi1987-operational-check.csv"),
                stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

# The two blocks differ by ten orders of magnitude, so the differences are
# formatted as strings rather than left to the table's numeric printing, which
# would render machine epsilon as a wall of zeros.
fmt_diff <- function(x) ifelse(is.na(x), "", formatC(x, format = "g", digits = 3))

blk1 <- data.frame(
  Check = "against cffdrs",
  Component = val$component,
  n = format(val$n, big.mark = ","),
  `Max absolute difference` = fmt_diff(val$max_abs_diff),
  `Mean absolute difference` = fmt_diff(val$mean_abs_diff),
  `Correlation` = "",
  check.names = FALSE)

# The data mart names the operational columns in full; the initials are the
# component names used everywhere else in this document.
initials <- function(x) vapply(strsplit(x, "_"),
                               function(p) paste0(substr(p, 1, 1), collapse = ""),
                               character(1))
op_agg <- do.call(rbind, lapply(split(opc, opc$component), function(d) {
  data.frame(
    Check = "against operational codes",
    Component = initials(d$component[1]),
    n = format(sum(d$n), big.mark = ","),
    `Max absolute difference` = "",
    `Mean absolute difference` = fmt_diff(weighted.mean(abs(d$mean_bias), d$n)),
    `Correlation` = formatC(weighted.mean(d$pearson_r, d$n), format = "f", digits = 4),
    check.names = FALSE)
}))
rownames(op_agg) <- NULL
fmt_tbl(rbind(blk1, op_agg))
```

```{r}
#| label: verify-prose
#| output: false
max_cffdrs <- max(val$max_abs_diff)
op_r <- weighted.mean(opc$pearson_r, opc$n)
# Station-days are counted once, not once per component compared: the rows
# are station-years per component, so sum within a component and take the largest.
op_n <- max(tapply(opc$n, opc$component, sum))
bias_of <- function(comp) {
  d <- opc[opc$component == comp, ]
  weighted.mean(abs(d$mean_bias), d$n)
}
r_of <- function(comp) {
  d <- opc[opc$component == comp, ]
  weighted.mean(d$pearson_r, d$n)
}
dc_bias <- bias_of("DROUGHT_CODE")
bui_bias <- bias_of("BUILDUP_INDEX")
ffmc_r <- r_of("FINE_FUEL_MOISTURE_CODE")
```

Over the Petawawa Research Forest test record, the FWI1987 implementation agreed with the CRAN package `cffdrs` to `r formatC(max_cffdrs, format = "g", digits = 2)` across all seven components (@tbl-verify). That was machine precision, because the two were the same arithmetic, so the check confirmed the transcription and not the equations themselves.

At the Okanagan stations, against the FWI1987 codes BC Wildfire Service computed at the time, the weighted mean correlation over `r n_fmt(op_n)` station-days was `r round(op_r, 3)`. The one large disagreement was a mean absolute bias of `r round(dc_bias, 0)` units in the Drought Code and `r round(bui_bias, 1)` in the Buildup Index computed partly from it. BC Wildfire Service overwintered the Drought Code, keeping the previous autumn's value as the spring starting value, whereas this study restarted it at 15 on 1 April. The difference was one of convention, in the known direction that a restarted Drought Code is lower than an overwintered one. It entered every absolute Drought Code and Buildup Index value reported here but no comparison between the three series, which all restarted identically.

The Fine Fuel Moisture Code, on which the version comparison principally depended, correlated `r round(opc$pearson_r[opc$component == "FINE_FUEL_MOISTURE_CODE"] |> weighted.mean(opc$n[opc$component == "FINE_FUEL_MOISTURE_CODE"]), 4)` with the operational value.

## A.3 Summary Hour Sensitivity {.unnumbered}

```{r}
#| label: tbl-sensitivity
#| tbl-cap: "Sensitivity of the absolute extreme-day counts to how an hourly series is reduced to a daily value. The fixed hour is 16:00 Local Standard Time, 17:00 local daylight time. The daily maximum takes the largest of the 24 hourly values, which must be at least as large and is reported only to bound the effect of the choice. FWI1987 produces one value per day and so appears once."
sens_cols <- c("n_ffmc_ge91", "n_ffmc_max_ge91", "n_fwi_ge19", "n_fwi_max_ge19")
have <- sens_cols %in% names(metrics)
if (all(have)) {
  sens <- do.call(rbind, lapply(split(metrics, metrics$series), function(d) data.frame(
    Series = unname(SERIES[d$series[1]]),
    `Days FFMC >= 91, fixed hour` = round(mean(d$n_ffmc_ge91, na.rm = TRUE), 1),
    `Days FFMC >= 91, daily maximum` = round(mean(d$n_ffmc_max_ge91, na.rm = TRUE), 1),
    `Days FWI >= 19, fixed hour` = round(mean(d$n_fwi_ge19, na.rm = TRUE), 1),
    `Days FWI >= 19, daily maximum` = round(mean(d$n_fwi_max_ge19, na.rm = TRUE), 1),
    check.names = FALSE)))
  rownames(sens) <- NULL
  fmt_tbl(sens)
} else {
  stop("seasonal-metrics.csv carries no daily maximum columns; re-run build_seasonal_metrics.py")
}
```

Over the study record, @tbl-sensitivity bounds the effect of reducing an hourly series to one daily value. Taking the daily maximum of the 24 hourly values instead of the value at one fixed hour raised every count in the two FWI2025 series. That rule was not the primary summary, because part of the rise came from taking the largest of 24 values and not from the System.

# Data Availability {.unnumbered}

The hourly fire weather observations are public at the BC Wildfire Service Weather Data Mart [@bcws2026datamart] and the incident record, the station locations and the basin boundary at the BC Data Catalogue [@bcws2026incidents; @bcws2026stations; @geobc2026fwagroups], all under the licences stated at those sources. The FWI2025 calculation used the Canadian Forest Service reference implementation [@nrcan2026cffdrsng] unmodified. The derived tables, the FWI1987 implementation, the retrieval and analysis code, and the source of this document, from which every number in it is computed, are available from the author and will be archived with a persistent identifier on acceptance. The hourly record was retrieved from the BC Wildfire Service Weather Data Mart, whose FTP server the Service states "will be reaching the end of it's lifespan by January 2027" [@bcws2026datamart], so the retrieved record is deposited with the code.

```{r}
days over the record, and lightning ignition skill differed by %.4f. Trends

stated.\n",
  num_word(n_stations_kept), format(n_kept, big.mark = ","), n_seasons, yr_first, yr_last,

# The front matter reads this file, so the abstract prints at the head of the
```

```{python}
#| label: verify-quotations
#| output: false
"""Check every quotation from GLC-X-42 in the manuscript against the report itself.

Written 2026-08-15. The project convention is that a source is quoted verbatim and
the quotation is checked against the source, because a paraphrase attributed as a
quotation survives drafts unnoticed. A sibling manuscript in this library spent
several drafts attributing the word "additive" to an abstract in which it never
appears, and the error survived because nobody opened the PDF and searched it.

This script opens the PDF and searches it. Each quotation below is the exact
string the manuscript puts inside quotation marks, paired with the section the
manuscript attributes it to. The comparison runs against the extracted text layer
with line-break hyphenation repaired and whitespace collapsed, because a PDF
breaks words across lines and a naive search would fail on formatting rather than
on substance. Case is significant: the check is exact.

The check earned its keep on first run. The manuscript had
"using hourly weather to better reflect maximum burning conditions" with a lower
case u, taken from a project note rather than from the report. The report's first
bullet under "Key updates include" reads "Using hourly weather to better reflect
maximum burning conditions." The substance was right and the transcription was
not, which is precisely the class of error this check exists to find.

Writes ``02.inputs/derived/quotation-verification.csv``, committed. Exits non-zero
if any quotation fails, so it can gate a build.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import os
import re
import sys

import pandas as pd
import pypdf

ROOT = os.path.abspath("..")
PDF = os.path.join(ROOT, "04.references", "standards",
                   "CFS-FireDangerGroup-2025-GLC-X-42-FWI2025.pdf")

# (quotation as the manuscript prints it, section the manuscript attributes it to)
QUOTATIONS = [
    ("Using hourly weather to better reflect maximum burning conditions",
     "section 1, executive summary, first key update"),
    ("the time lag function used in the FWI2025 for the FFMC has been cut in half",
     "section 4.1.1"),
    ("an FFMC of 91 in FWI1987 should correspond to an FFMC of approximately 91 in FWI2025",
     "section 4.1"),
    ("should reflect meaningful differences in fuel moisture content",
     "section 4.1"),
    ("calculations always use hourly weather",
     "section 3.1.1.1"),
    ("a single daily weather observation from approximately solar noon",
     "section 3.1"),
    ("numerical weather model outputs are not strictly the same as point observations "
     "of weather from a weather station",
     "Appendix C-1"),
    ("At the grid cell scale, outputs from numerical models typically represent what can "
     "be thought of as average conditions across that cell",
     "Appendix C-1"),
    ("start calculation three days after the disappearance of snow cover",
     "Appendix C-2.3"),
]


def normalise(text: str) -> str:
    """Repair line-break hyphenation and collapse whitespace, changing nothing else."""
    text = re.sub(r"-\s*\n\s*", "", text)
    return re.sub(r"\s+", " ", text)


def main() -> None:
    if not os.path.exists(PDF):
        sys.exit(f"The report is not in the tree at {PDF}. "
                 "04.references/README.md records how to retrieve it.")

    reader = pypdf.PdfReader(PDF)
    pages = [p.extract_text() or "" for p in reader.pages]
    whole = normalise("\n".join(pages))

    rows = []
    failures = 0
    for quote, attribution in QUOTATIONS:
        q = normalise(quote)
        found = q in whole
        page = None
        if found:
            for i, p in enumerate(pages, start=1):
                if q in normalise(p):
                    page = i
                    break
        rows.append({
            "quotation": quote,
            "attributed_to": attribution,
            "found_verbatim": found,
            "pdf_page": page,
        })
        if not found:
            failures += 1
        print(f"{'OK  ' if found else 'FAIL'}  p{page if page else '--':>3}  "
              f"{quote[:72]}", flush=True)

    dest = os.path.join(ROOT, "02.inputs", "derived", "quotation-verification.csv")
    pd.DataFrame(rows).to_csv(dest, index=False)
    print(f"\n{len(QUOTATIONS) - failures} of {len(QUOTATIONS)} verified verbatim")
    print(f"Wrote {dest}")

    if failures:
        sys.exit(f"{failures} quotation(s) do not appear in the source as written.")


if not os.path.exists(os.path.join(ROOT, "02.inputs", "derived", "quotation-verification.csv")):
    main()
```

```{python}
#| label: verify-literature-quotations
#| output: false
"""Check every direct quotation the manuscript attributes to a source other than
the 2025 FWI System report against that source's own text.

Written 2026-09-12, the sibling of the chunk above, which covers the 2025
report alone. The manuscript is read, every passage in double quotation marks is
paired with the citation that follows it in the same sentence, and the passage is
searched for in the source. The source text is the PDF saved as
04.references/literature/<key>.pdf, extracted with pdftotext, or a saved page or
text at 04.references/literature/<key>.html, .md or .txt, or, for the two web
pages in REPORTS, the capture saved under 04.references/reports/, or, for a source
read from its abstract only, the abstract returned by CrossRef or OpenAlex for the
DOI in references.bib. Extended 2026-10-13 for the sources the literature review
added. Comparison is on letters and digits only, so wording must
match exactly while quotation marks, dashes, ligatures, spacing and line-break
hyphenation are ignored.

Writes 02.inputs/derived/literature-quotation-verification.csv and exits non-zero
if any quotation is not found.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import csv
import html
import json
import os
import re
import subprocess
import sys
import time
import urllib.parse
import urllib.request

ROOT = os.path.abspath("..")
QMD = os.path.join(ROOT, "01.manuscript", "manuscript.qmd")
BIB = os.path.join(ROOT, "04.references", "references.bib")
LIT = os.path.join(ROOT, "04.references", "literature")
OUT = os.path.join(ROOT, "02.inputs", "derived", "literature-quotation-verification.csv")
# Catalogue records are read through the catalogue API.
CATALOGUE = {"bcws2026psta": "bc-wildfire-psta-head-fire-intensity",
             "bcws2026stations": "bc-wildfire-active-weather-stations"}
UA = {"User-Agent": "forest-fire-index-trends/1.0"}
# Web pages quoted in the manuscript, read from the captures saved on the date in
# their file names. Added 2026-10-13.
REPORTS = {"nrcan2026cffdrsng": os.path.join(ROOT, "04.references", "reports", "cffdrs-ng", "README-2026-10-13.md"),
           "bcws2026datamart": os.path.join(ROOT, "04.references", "reports", "bcws", "predictive-services-page-2026-10-13.html")}



def pdf_text(path: str) -> str:
    """pdftotext output with running headers and footers removed, so that a
    sentence a page break interrupts still reads as one. A line that repeats on
    three or more pages, or that is a bare DOI link, is a header or footer."""
    import collections
    raw = subprocess.run(["pdftotext", path, "-"], capture_output=True, text=True).stdout
    pages = raw.split("\f")
    seen = collections.Counter(l.strip() for pg in pages for l in set(pg.split("\n")) if l.strip())
    keep = []
    for pg in pages:
        for l in pg.split("\n"):
            t = l.strip()
            if t and (seen[t] >= 3 or re.match(r"^https?://doi\.org/\S+$", t)):
                continue
            keep.append(l)
    return "\n".join(keep)

def text_of(path: str) -> str:
    """Plain text of a saved source: pdftotext for a PDF, tags stripped and
    entities unescaped for a page, the file as read for anything else."""
    if path.endswith(".pdf"):
        return subprocess.run(["pdftotext", path, "-"], capture_output=True, text=True).stdout
    raw = open(path, encoding="utf-8", errors="ignore").read()
    if path.endswith((".html", ".htm")):
        raw = html.unescape(re.sub(r"<[^>]+>", " ", raw))
    return raw


def letters(s: str) -> str:
    s = s.replace("ﬁ", "fi").replace("ﬂ", "fl")
    return re.sub(r"[^a-z0-9]", "", s.lower())


def get_json(url: str) -> dict | None:
    for _ in range(3):
        try:
            req = urllib.request.Request(url, headers=UA)
            with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=45) as r:
                return json.load(r)
        except Exception:
            time.sleep(3)
    return None


def abstract_for(doi: str) -> str:
    cr = get_json("https://api.crossref.org/works/" + urllib.parse.quote(doi))
    text = (cr or {}).get("message", {}).get("abstract", "") if cr else ""
    oa = get_json("https://api.openalex.org/works/doi:" + urllib.parse.quote(doi))
    inv = (oa or {}).get("abstract_inverted_index") or {}
    pos = {i: w for w, idx in inv.items() for i in idx}
    return text + " " + " ".join(pos[i] for i in sorted(pos))


def main() -> None:
    qmd = open(QMD, encoding="utf-8").read()
    prose = re.sub(r"```\{(?:r|python)\}.*?\n```", "", qmd, flags=re.S)
    prose = re.sub(r"^---\n.*?\n---\n", "", prose, count=1, flags=re.S)
    # Inline R expressions are code, not quotation.
    prose = re.sub(r"`r [^`]*`", "N", prose)
    # Quotations from the 2025 report are recorded here against the report's own
    # text as well, so that quotations added after verify_quotations.py was written
    # are not left unchecked.
    glc = os.path.join(ROOT, "04.references", "standards", "CFS-FireDangerGroup-2025-GLC-X-42-FWI2025.pdf")
    glc_text = letters(subprocess.run(["pdftotext", glc, "-"], capture_output=True, text=True).stdout) if os.path.exists(glc) else ""
    bib = open(BIB, encoding="utf-8").read()
    dois = {k: d for k, d in re.findall(r"@\w+\{([^,]+),[^@]*?doi\s*=\s*[{\"]([^}\"]+)", bib, flags=re.S | re.I)}

    # A quotation is paired with the first citation key after it in its sentence.
    pairs = []
    prev_keys: list[str] = []
    for sent in re.split(r"(?<=[.?!])\s+(?=[A-Z@])", prose):
        for m in re.finditer(r'"([^"]{12,})"', sent):
            # A quotation of four words or fewer is a name, not a passage.
            if len(m.group(1).split()) < 5 and not re.search(r"@\w+, p\.", sent[m.end():m.end() + 40]):
                continue
            if glc_text and letters(m.group(1)) in glc_text:
                pairs.append(("cffdg2025fwi2025", m.group(1)))
                continue
            after = sent[m.end():]
            # The key after the quotation in its sentence, or, failing that, the
            # nearest key before it, since a sentence may cite two sources in turn.
            k = re.search(r"@([a-z][a-z0-9]+)", after)
            before = re.findall(r"@([a-z][a-z0-9]+)", sent[:m.start()])
            # A sentence that quotes a study named in the sentence before it,
            # "@author found X. They reported that "...".", takes that key.
            if not k and not before:
                before = prev_keys
            if not k and not before:
                continue
            key = k.group(1) if k else before[-1]
            if key.startswith(("tbl", "fig", "sec")):
                continue
            pairs.append((key, m.group(1)))
        prev_keys = re.findall(r"@([a-z][a-z0-9]+)", sent) or prev_keys

    cache: dict[str, str] = {}
    rows, failed = [], 0
    for key, quote in pairs:
        if key not in cache:
            pdf = os.path.join(LIT, key + ".pdf")
            if key == "cffdg2025fwi2025":
                cache[key] = subprocess.run(["pdftotext", glc, "-"], capture_output=True, text=True).stdout
                src = "2025 report pdf"
            elif key in CATALOGUE:
                j = get_json("https://catalogue.data.gov.bc.ca/api/3/action/package_show?id=" + CATALOGUE[key])
                cache[key] = ((j or {}).get("result") or {}).get("notes", "")
                src = "catalogue record"
            elif os.path.exists(pdf):
                cache[key] = pdf_text(pdf)
                src = "pdf"
            elif any(os.path.exists(os.path.join(LIT, key + ext)) for ext in (".html", ".md", ".txt")):
                ext = next(e for e in (".html", ".md", ".txt") if os.path.exists(os.path.join(LIT, key + e)))
                cache[key] = text_of(os.path.join(LIT, key + ext))
                src = "saved text"
            elif key in REPORTS and os.path.exists(REPORTS[key]):
                cache[key] = text_of(REPORTS[key])
                src = "saved page"
            elif key in dois:
                cache[key] = abstract_for(dois[key])
                src = "abstract"
            else:
                cache[key] = ""
                src = "no source text"
            cache[key + "::src"] = src
        found = letters(quote) in letters(cache[key])
        failed += not found
        rows.append({"key": key, "quotation": quote, "source_text": cache[key + "::src"], "found_verbatim": found})
        print(f"{'ok  ' if found else 'FAIL'}  {key:32s} {quote[:70]}")

    with open(OUT, "w", newline="", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        w = csv.DictWriter(f, fieldnames=["key", "quotation", "source_text", "found_verbatim"])
        w.writeheader()
        w.writerows(rows)
    print(f"\n{len(rows)} quotations checked, {failed} not found. Wrote {OUT}")
    if failed:
        raise SystemExit(f"{failed} quotation(s) not found verbatim")


if not os.path.exists(OUT):
    main()
```

```{python}
#| label: verify-references
#| output: false
"""Verify every candidate citation against Crossref before it enters the bibliography.

Written 2026-08-15. The project convention is that a bibliography entry is taken
from the registry and never from memory, because a DOI recalled from memory
resolves to the wrong paper often enough to be dangerous and the error is
invisible until a referee follows it. This project has already recorded two such
failures.

The script takes a candidate list of works, each with the title as remembered and
either a DOI as remembered or nothing. For each it does two things. It asks
Crossref to resolve the DOI, if one was offered, and compares the title that
comes back against the title that was offered. Separately, and regardless, it
searches Crossref for the offered title and reports the best match with its
score. A candidate is only usable when both agree.

Similarity is a token overlap on lowercased alphanumeric words, which is crude
but sufficient to catch the failure that matters: a DOI that resolves to an
entirely different paper.

Writes ``02.inputs/derived/reference-verification.csv``, committed, and prints
Crossref's own BibTeX for every candidate that passed, ready to paste into
``04.references/references.bib``.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import os
import re
import sys
import time

import pandas as pd
import requests

MAILTO = "seamusrobertmurphy@gmail.com"

# Government and agency dataset entries in references.bib (keys geobc2026*,
# bcws2026*, wsc2026subsubdrainage, bc2026municipalities, aws2026terraintiles,
# nrcan2026cffdrsng, wang2026cffdrspkg) have no DOI and are outside this check;
# their titles and owners were read from the BC Data Catalogue API on
# 2026-09-12 and are recorded in 02.inputs/README.md.

# Candidates. The title is what is being claimed; the DOI is what is being
# tested. Nothing here is trusted until Crossref agrees with it.
CANDIDATES = [
    # Added 2026-09-12 for the literature revisions (Revisions 1, 4, 7, 10, 13).
    # Titles as returned by CrossRef for each DOI on that date.
    ('Techniques of trend analysis for monthly water quality data',

     '10.5194/nhess-14-1477-2014'),
    ('Climate-induced variations in global wildfire danger from 1979 to 2013',
     '10.1038/ncomms8537'),
    ('To prewhiten or not to prewhiten in trend analysis?',
     '10.1623/hysj.52.4.611'),
    ('The influence of autocorrelation on the ability to detect trend in hydrological series',
     '10.1002/hyp.1095'),
    ('Block bootstrap for Mann–Kendall trend test of serially dependent data',
     '10.1002/hyp.8438'),
    ('The control of the false discovery rate in multiple testing under dependency',
     '10.1214/aos/1013699998'),
    ('“The Stippling Shows Statistically Significant Grid Points”: How Research Results are Routinely Overstated and Overinterpreted, and What to Do about It',
     '10.1175/bams-d-15-00267.1'),
    ('Resampling Hypothesis Tests for Autocorrelated Fields',
     '10.1175/1520-0442(1997)010<0065:rhtfaf>2.0.co;2'),
    ('The Jackknife and the Bootstrap for General Stationary Observations',
     '10.1214/aos/1176347265'),

     '10.1080/01621459.1994.10476870'),

     '10.1080/01621459.1987.10478410'),

     '10.1214/ss/1032280214'),

    ('Statistical significance of trends and trend differences in layer‐average atmospheric temperature time series',
     '10.1029/1999jd901105'),

     '10.1175/jcli3366.1'),
    ('Factors affecting the detection of trends: Statistical considerations and applications to environmental data',

def norm(s: str) -> set[str]:
    return set(re.findall(r"[a-z0-9]+", (s or "").lower())) - {
        "the", "a", "an", "of", "for", "in", "to", "and", "on", "with"
    }


def similarity(a: str, b: str) -> float:
    x, y = norm(a), norm(b)
    return len(x & y) / max(len(x | y), 1)


def get(url: str, **params) -> dict | None:
    for attempt in range(3):
        try:
            r = requests.get(url, params=params, headers={"User-Agent": UA}, timeout=45)
            if r.status_code == 404:
                return None
            r.raise_for_status()
            return r.json()
        except Exception:
            if attempt == 2:
                return None
            time.sleep(3)
    return None


def bibtex(doi: str) -> str | None:
    try:
        r = requests.get(
            f"https://doi.org/{doi}",
            headers={"Accept": "application/x-bibtex", "User-Agent": UA},
            timeout=45,
        )
        return r.text.strip() if r.ok else None
    except Exception:
        return None


def main() -> None:
    root = os.path.abspath("..")
    rows = []
    passed = []

    for claimed_title, claimed_doi in CANDIDATES:
        rec = {"claimed_title": claimed_title, "claimed_doi": claimed_doi}

        # 1. Does the offered DOI resolve, and to this paper?
        if claimed_doi:
            j = get(f"https://api.crossref.org/works/{claimed_doi}")
            if j is None:
                rec.update(doi_resolves=False, doi_title=None, doi_title_similarity=None)
            else:
                m = j["message"]
                t = (m.get("title") or [""])[0]
                rec.update(
                    doi_resolves=True,
                    doi_title=t,
                    doi_title_similarity=round(similarity(claimed_title, t), 3),
                )
        else:
            rec.update(doi_resolves=None, doi_title=None, doi_title_similarity=None)

        # 2. Independently, what does Crossref return for the title?
        j = get("https://api.crossref.org/works", **{
            "query.bibliographic": claimed_title, "rows": 3, "mailto": MAILTO
        })
        best_doi = best_title = None
        if j and j["message"]["items"]:
            items = j["message"]["items"]
            # Prefer the version of record. Crossref frequently ranks a preprint
            # above the journal article that superseded it, and the project
            # convention is that a preprint is distinguished from a peer reviewed
            # source rather than silently substituted for one.
            article = [
                x for x in items
                if x.get("type") in ("journal-article", "proceedings-article")
                and similarity(claimed_title, (x.get("title") or [""])[0]) >= 0.7
            ]
            it = article[0] if article else items[0]
            rec["search_type"] = it.get("type")
            best_doi = it.get("DOI")
            best_title = (it.get("title") or [""])[0]
            rec.update(
                search_doi=best_doi,
                search_title=best_title,
                search_title_similarity=round(similarity(claimed_title, best_title), 3),
                search_year=(it.get("issued", {}).get("date-parts", [[None]])[0][0]),
                search_container=(it.get("container-title") or [""])[0],
            )

        agree = (
            claimed_doi and rec.get("doi_title_similarity", 0) is not None
            and (rec.get("doi_title_similarity") or 0) >= 0.7
        ) or (
            not claimed_doi and (rec.get("search_title_similarity") or 0) >= 0.8
        )
        rec["verdict"] = "verified" if agree else "REJECTED"
        chosen = claimed_doi if (claimed_doi and (rec.get("doi_title_similarity") or 0) >= 0.7) else best_doi
        rec["chosen_doi"] = chosen if agree else None
        rows.append(rec)
        if agree and chosen:
            passed.append((claimed_title, chosen))

        print(f"{rec['verdict']:9s}  {claimed_title[:64]:64s}  -> {rec['chosen_doi']}", flush=True)

    df = pd.DataFrame(rows)
    dest = os.path.join(root, "02.inputs", "derived", "reference-verification.csv")
    df.to_csv(dest, index=False)
    print(f"\nWrote {dest}")
    print(f"Verified {len(passed)} of {len(CANDIDATES)} candidates\n")

    print("=" * 70)
    print("BibTeX from Crossref for the verified entries")
    print("=" * 70)
    for title, doi in passed:
        bt = bibtex(doi)
        print(f"\n% verified against Crossref {time.strftime('%Y-%m-%d')}; "
              f"title matched: {title}")
        print(bt if bt else f"% BibTeX retrieval failed for {doi}")


if not os.path.exists(os.path.join("..", "02.inputs", "derived", "reference-verification.csv")):
    main()
```

```{r}
# Everything the root README shows is written out here, from the same objects the
# document displayed, so the README cannot drift from the manuscript. It is a
# view of this render, not a second telling of it.
tbl_dir <- file.path(outputs, "tables")
fig_dir <- file.path(outputs, "figures")
dir.create(tbl_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
dir.create(fig_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

writeLines(abstract_text, file.path(outputs, "abstract.txt"))
meta_or <- function(field, fallback) {
  v <- tryCatch(rmarkdown::metadata[[field]], error = function(e) NULL)
  if (is.null(v) || !nzchar(v)) fallback else v
}
writeLines(meta_or("title",
  "Fire danger trends across the 2025 update to the Canadian Fire Weather Index System in the Okanagan basin"),
  file.path(outputs, "title.txt"))
writeLines(meta_or("subtitle", ""), file.path(outputs, "subtitle.txt"))

# Table label, the data frame the table was built from, and its caption. The
# captions are repeated here rather than parsed back out of the chunk options,
# which is the one duplication in this file and is why they are kept short.
# A table that its own chunk did not build is skipped rather than faked; the
# README then simply does not show it, which is visible, instead of showing an
# empty frame, which is not.
if (!exists("ct")) ct <- NULL
if (!exists("sens")) sens <- NULL

EXPORTS <- list(
  list("tbl-stations", agg, "The weather record. Coverage is the share of the 1 April to 30 September hours in which temperature, humidity and wind were all observed, before any gap filling."),
  list("tbl-completeness", cd, "Completeness of the ignition record by decade. Both dating and cause attribution fall sharply after 2000."),
  list("tbl-verify", rbind(blk1, op_agg), "Verification of the FWI1987 implementation against the CRAN package cffdrs and against the codes BC Wildfire Service computed operationally."),
  list("tbl-thresholds", tp, "Where each absolute threshold falls in each series' own 1991 to 2020 reference distribution."),
  list("tbl-capability", ct, "The two quantities FWI2025 reports and FWI1987 cannot: when peak burning conditions occur and how long the burning window stays open."),
  list("tbl-trends", tr, "Theil-Sen slopes per season for each seasonal metric under each series, pooled across stations."),
  list("tbl-slopediff", sd_tab, "Difference in Theil-Sen slope between series, by metric and contrast, with paired bootstrap intervals."),
  list("tbl-sensitivity", sens, "Sensitivity of the absolute extreme-day counts to how an hourly series is reduced to a daily value."),
  list("tbl-ignition", it, "Negative binomial models of daily ignition counts on daily basin Fire Weather Index."),
  list("tbl-stationarity", st, "Test of whether the within-season danger to ignition relationship changes across the record."),
  list("tbl-shift", sh, "How each change moved the level of each metric, in its own unit."),
  list("tbl-limits", lim, "What a window of this length can and cannot resolve.")
)
for (e in EXPORTS) {
  if (is.null(e[[2]]) || !nrow(e[[2]])) next
  write.csv(e[[2]], file.path(tbl_dir, paste0(e[[1]], ".csv")), row.names = FALSE)
  writeLines(e[[3]], file.path(tbl_dir, paste0(e[[1]], ".caption.txt")))
}
```
